units.passage: Data Protection: Ethical AI tools prioritize data security and implement measures to protect user information from unauthorized access or misuse.
units.policy: Ethical AI tools prioritize data security and implement measures to protect user information from unauthorized access or misuse.
units.why: "Ethical AI tools prioritize data security and implement measures to protect user information" is a data-protection criterion for choosing tools, P50.
units.fit_note: Coder A: Describes a criterion for tool selection rather than telling students to protect their data. | Coder B: A criterion for tool choice, not an instruction to protect one's own data.

units.passage: It is also important to remove all identifying information before the work is shared with an AI platform to avoid violating FERPA.
units.why: "remove all identifying information before the work is shared with an AI platform to avoid violating FERPA" is a student-data privacy rule for instructors, so P50.
units.fit_note: Concerns student records shared with a detector, not personal data typed in by users.

units.passage: Data Privacy: Sensitive information belonging to USC and/or members of its community is improperly exposed to third parties;
units.why: The Data Privacy risk ("Sensitive information... is improperly exposed to third parties") warns about data exposure, so P50.

units.passage: The use of Public data with any AI Tool;
units.policy: Using Public data with any AI Tool is pre-authorized and does not require review.
units.why: "The use of Public data with any AI Tool" is pre-authorized without review, a permitted data use, so P50 (data rules) is nearest.
units.fit_note: Permission rather than protection: says which data may be used without review.

units.passage: The use of (1) Internal-Use Only or (2) Confidential data with a USC Enterprise AI Tool; or
units.policy: Using Internal-Use Only or Confidential data with a USC Enterprise AI Tool is pre-authorized and does not require review.
units.why: Using Internal-Use Only or Confidential data "with a USC Enterprise AI Tool" is pre-authorized; a data-and-vetted-tool permission, so P50.
units.fit_note: A permission tied to approved tools, not a protection rule.

units.passage: within USC locally hosted AI tools where data does not leave the local environment.
units.policy: Using Internal-Use Only or Confidential data within USC locally hosted AI tools where data does not leave the local environment is pre-authorized and does not require review.
units.why: Using such data in locally hosted tools "where data does not leave the local environment" is pre-authorized, so P50.
units.fit_note: A permission tied to local hosting.

units.passage: ​The use of Confidential – Controlled data with any AI Tool;
units.why: 'The use of Confidential - Controlled data with any AI Tool' is listed as prohibited, a data-protection ban on entering controlled data into AI: P50 (must-not) rather than P20 because the ban is about data class, not assignment materials.
units.fit_note: Prohibition may be lifted with documented approval from three offices.

units.passage: Automatically transmit USC data to external systems or third parties except as expressly permitted by University policy and applicable agreements; or
units.policy: Covered Individuals may not deploy or utilize Agentic AI systems that automatically transmit USC data to external systems or third parties except as expressly permitted by University policy and applicable agreements.
units.why: Agents may not "Automatically transmit USC data to external systems or third parties" except as policy permits, a data limit, so P50.

units.passage: Sharing student work and data with AI detectors also brings up serious ethical considerations for privacy, intellectual property, and adding student work to AI training materials.
units.policy: Sharing student work and data with AI detectors raises serious ethical considerations for privacy, intellectual property, and adding student work to AI training materials.
units.why: Warns that 'Sharing student work and data with AI detectors' raises privacy and IP concerns. P50 (protect personal data) is nearest; P49 is about students uploading course materials.
units.fit_note: Concerns student work given to detectors by staff, covering IP and AI training use as well as privacy. | A privacy and IP concern specifically about uploading student work to detectors

units.passage: All students need equitable access to key resources when GAI is taught or used as well as guidance on protecting their own and others’ privacy and data.
units.policy: All students need guidance on protecting their own and others' privacy and data when GAI is taught or used.
units.why: The second half of 'All students need equitable access to key resources ... as well as guidance on protecting their own and others' privacy and data' states a separate principle: students need privacy and data-protection guidance (P50). Coder A had put both halves in one P51 unit; the codebook requires one rule per unit.

units.passage: Share university resources for students that explain best practices for protecting their privacy, as well as personal and university data when using GAI tools.
units.policy: Instructors share university resources for students that explain best practices for protecting their privacy, as well as personal and university data when using GAI tools.
units.why: Asks instructors to 'Share university resources ... for protecting their privacy, as well as personal and university data', a data-protection practice (P50).

units.passage: First, instructors should be mindful that the submission of student work to a third-party detection tool could lead to risks associated with the violation of students’ intellectual property rights, FERPA, and perhaps HIPAA.
units.why: "instructors should be mindful that the submission of student work to a third-party detection tool could lead to risks associated with the violation of students' intellectual property rights, FERPA, and perhaps HIPAA" warns instructors about privacy and IP risk; "should be mindful" is should, P50 (protect personal data).
units.fit_note: Warns instructors about IP and FERPA/HIPAA risks of sending student work to detectors.

units.passage: If the AI tool is used to summarize identifiable data, there are serious DEI, privacy, and data security concerns.
units.why: The passage warns that using an AI tool "to summarize identifiable data" raises "serious DEI, privacy, and data security concerns", a data-protection caution (P50).
units.fit_note: Concern about uses of a planned institutional tool, not a formal review-and-approval procedure.

units.passage: Informally, students may subscribe to an AI tool, like ChatGPT, and not realize what rights they are giving up (e.g., tracking of browsing history, inputs into the AI tool, tracking of location by IP address).
units.why: The report says students "may subscribe to an AI tool, like ChatGPT, and not realize what rights they are giving up", a privacy warning about what tools collect (P50).

units.passage: For faculty and academic staff, unintentionally breaching data privacy may bring with it serious consequences both for them and for the university.
units.why: The report warns that "unintentionally breaching data privacy" may have serious consequences for faculty, staff and the university, a privacy caution for employees (P50).

units.passage: Understanding the terms of use that one is presented with when first signing up to use an AI tool or system presents another challenge, especially given the technical jargon and organization of the documentation.
units.why: The report notes that terms of use are hard to understand "given the technical jargon", so users cannot easily judge data risks; a privacy caution about signing up for tools, closest to P50.

units.passage: Moreover, if the university offers an AI tool or system, it will have been vetted for privacy considerations, data integrity and data security.
units.why: The CIO's rationale is that "if the university offers an AI tool or system, it will have been vetted for privacy considerations, data integrity and data security", preferring vetted tools (P50).

units.passage: ChatGPT for example, will take the prompts and add it to the training data. This feature is defaulted to be “on”. Confidential data can thus be compromised. ChatGPT has a setting to turn this off.
units.why: The Chief Privacy Officer observes ChatGPT will "take the prompts and add it to the training data", defaulted to on, so "confidential data can thus be compromised"; a data-protection warning (P50).

units.passage: The need for users to avoid entering personal information, their own or someone else’s, is perhaps one of the top cautions we can offer.
units.why: The report says "the need for users to avoid entering personal information, their own or someone else's, is perhaps one of the top cautions", a ban on personal data entry (P50).

units.passage: This is especially important for our students, who may be exploited by technology companies with the guise of saving time, but in fact who are mining private information from our students.
units.why: Students 'may be exploited by technology companies with the guise of saving time', a harm warning (P50).

units.passage: When using AI tools–including detection tools–uploading student work and/or Personally Identifiable Information may violate our University’s Generative AI Usage Policy
units.why: 'uploading student work and/or Personally Identifiable Information may violate our University's Generative AI Usage Policy' warns instructors against putting student work or PII into AI or detection tools; P50, instructor, during-work, should-not.

units.passage: Only information classified as “Public” may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools (see Appendix).
units.why: 'Only information classified as “Public” may be entered into publicly available generative AI tools' limits what data can go into public AI tools; P50, all, during-work, must-not (for non-Public data).

units.passage: If the tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as “Sensitive” into the generative AI tool.
units.policy: If a generative AI tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as Sensitive into it.
units.why: 'If the tool has been reviewed and approved by Wesleyan ITS, users may enter information classified as "Sensitive"' permits Sensitive data in ITS-approved tools. It binds all users while they use AI (during-work), permits (may), and is a data-protection rule tied to vetted tools (P50).
units.fit_note: Permits Sensitive data in approved tools; framed as a data rule rather than a general duty to use approved tools.

units.passage: Any information classified as “Restricted” cannot be entered into any generative AI tool without explicit written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and the relevant Cabinet member.
units.policy: Information classified as Restricted cannot be entered into any generative AI tool without explicit written approval from the Chief Information Security Officer and the relevant Cabinet member.
units.why: 'Any information classified as “Restricted” cannot be entered into any generative AI tool without explicit written approval' bars Restricted data absent approval from the CISO and Cabinet member; P50, all, must-not.
units.fit_note: A: Also requires named written approvers; P107 (prior approval) was not chosen because the approval concerns data, not AI use generally. B: Mainly a data rule; classed here for the named approvers and exception route.

units.passage: As defined by the Data Classification Policy , Public Data can be used in any publicly available generative AI tool. This includes but is not limited to: Open AI ChatGPT (all versions) Anthropic Claude (Individual plans) As defined by the Data Classification Policy, Sensitive Data can only be used in the following generative AI tool: Open AI ChatGPT Enterprise and Business Anthropic Claude Team and Enterprise Zoom AI Companion (Wesleyan license only) Microsoft Copilot (Wesleyan license only) Google Gemini (Wesleyan license only) As defined by the Data Classification Policy, Restricted Data cannot be used by any generative AI tools without prior approval.
units.why: The appendix says 'Restricted Data cannot be used by any generative AI tools without prior approval', with FERPA information, SSNs and PHI as examples; P50, all, during-work, must-not.

units.passage: The university’s data classification policy provides direction regarding the privacy, security, and integrity of WCU data and outlines the responsibilities of institutional units and individuals for such data. To protect the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive data and prevent unauthorized disclosure or use, do not input any sensitive data into generative AI tools.
units.why: "Do not input any sensitive data into generative AI tools" is a data-protection prohibition that matches P50.

units.passage: When using generative AI tools, do not input any student records, grades, class rosters, or other educational information protected by FERPA.
units.why: FERPA rule: 'do not input any student records, grades, class rosters, or other educational information protected by FERPA'; protects personal data, P50.

units.passage: AI systems often record, and store data provided to them.
units.why: "AI systems often record, and store data provided to them" explains why data caution is needed (P50, informs).

units.passage: Entering any personally identifiable information (PII) such as names, email addresses, birthdates or ID numbers, into an AI platform could cause the tool to repeat this information as part of interactions with other users at a later time.
units.why: 'Entering any personally identifiable information (PII) ... could cause the tool to repeat this information' warns on PII exposure; P50.

units.passage: Extra caution should be taken with information regarding hiring, admissions, or evaluation of students or employees as it is often combined with other detailed personal and confidential information.
units.why: Extra caution advice 'regarding hiring, admissions, or evaluation of students or employees' is data-protection advice (P50), not a rule keeping humans in decisions about people (P73).

units.passage: You can share public data that is already accessible by the public with AI tools.
units.why: "You can share public data that is already accessible by the public with AI tools" is an explicit permission within the data rule (P50).

units.passage: Do NOT provide data to AI tools if any part of that data should not be included in future results provided by that system.
units.why: 'Do NOT provide data to AI tools if any part of that data should not be included in future results' is a data-input prohibition; P50.

units.passage: Do NOT share Confidential data or Sensitive data with AI tools unless that sharing has been specifically authorized.
units.why: "Do NOT share Confidential data or Sensitive data with AI tools unless that sharing has been specifically authorized" prohibits sharing categories of data, P50.

units.passage: Most common AI tools are not compliant with the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
units.why: "Most common AI tools are not compliant with FERPA, HIPAA and GDPR" is a fact backing the data rules (P50).

units.passage: Users must follow data privacy and security guidelines when using generative AI, protecting personal and institutional data.
units.why: 'Users must follow data privacy and security guidelines when using generative AI, protecting personal and institutional data'; P50.

units.passage: Ensure data privacy and security when using AI tools in daily tasks.
units.why: "Ensure data privacy and security when using AI tools in daily tasks" is a data duty for staff, P50.

units.passage: Caution should be used when choosing a third-party AI detection tools to avoid disclosing any protected information. Work submitted to these tools should be fully anonymized, per Interim Generative AI Guidelines from the State.
units.why: "Work submitted to these tools should be fully anonymized" protects student data when using detectors, P50.
units.fit_note: Header says do not share personally identifying information.

units.passage: Note that instructors should not submit sensitive, confidential, or any personally-identifiable data about students, to a generative AI system.
units.why: "instructors should not submit sensitive, confidential, or any personally-identifiable data about students, to a generative AI system" is a privacy rule, P50.

units.passage: Never use sensitive or personally-identifiable information (PII, educational records, or pre-published research).
units.why: Tells employees 'Never use sensitive or personally-identifiable information' in AI: privacy (P50).

units.passage: Members of the WPI community may be unaware that information entered into a generative AI tool immediately becomes part of the generative AI’s information database.
units.why: Warns that information entered into a generative AI tool 'immediately becomes part of the generative AI's information database', a fact explaining why the rule exists. P50 covers that tools retain prompts; informs, not a command.

units.passage: As a result, any private or confidential information entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public.
units.why: States that 'any private or confidential information entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public', the risk consequence behind the data rule. Rationale for P50; informs.

units.passage: Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Google Gemini, etc.).
units.why: 'Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools' is a direct ban on one kind of input, binding everyone: must-not. P50 fits best; P20 and P49 concern assignment materials or course content, not confidential institutional data.

units.passage: Do not enter confidential or legally restricted data or any data that Yale’s data classification policy identifies as moderate or high-risk into an AI tool.
units.why: "Do not enter confidential or legally restricted data" is a prohibition on what goes into AI tools, about data protection, so P50 (protect personal and confidential data), not P20 which concerns assignment specs and student code.

units.passage: Treat all information shared with an AI tool as if it will become public.
units.why: "Treat all information shared with an AI tool as if it will become public" is an instruction on privacy of inputs, matching P50 (AI tools store prompts; protect personal data).

units.passage: Do not share information that is personal or sensitive,
units.why: "Do not share information that is personal or sensitive" forbids putting personal or sensitive information into an AI tool, addressed to everyone: P50 (protect personal and confidential data) with must-not.

units.passage: Do not share information that is personal or sensitive, and be mindful that the information you input into an AI tool may be retained.
units.why: "be mindful that the information you input into an AI tool may be retained" warns that tools keep prompts, which P50 explicitly lists ("AI tools store prompts"); modality should because it asks for mindfulness.

units.passage: Instructors must safeguard student data, intellectual property, and autonomy when integrating AI tools into coursework.
units.why: "Instructors must safeguard student data, intellectual property, and autonomy when integrating AI tools into coursework" is a duty on instructors for data and IP, P50.

units.passage: Faculty and staff may not enter student work, grades, or personally identifiable student information into consumer AI tools.
units.why: "Faculty and staff may not enter student work, grades, or personally identifiable student information into consumer AI tools" protects student data (P50).

units.passage: Three key attributes of these tools are 1) the risk that an input could potentially become public, 2) the risk that the output may be biased, misleading, or inaccurate, and 3) the risk it may be used in phishing campaigns.
units.why: "the risk that an input could potentially become public" names a privacy risk of AI tools, P50.

units.passage: If Generative AI is given access to personal information, the technology may not respect the privacy rights of individuals, including in a manner that may be required for compliance with applicable data protection laws;
units.why: "the technology may not respect the privacy rights of individuals" explains the privacy risk of giving AI personal information (P50).

units.passage: YU faculty and staff must not input any information classified as Internal or Restricted into Generative AI tools, except when expressly permitted by ITS after confirming appropriate contract language and security controls.
units.why: "YU faculty and staff must not input any information classified as Internal or Restricted into Generative AI tools" bans entering confidential data (P50).

units.passage: must not input any information that is identifiable to a person, third party, or the
units.why: "must not input any information that is identifiable to a person, third party, or the University into a Generative AI tool" bans entering personal data (P50).

units.passage: Ask the Generative AI system not to use inputs for training the system: Some Generative AI systems permit users to opt out of the use of their data to train future iterations of the Generative AI system. Where that option is available, YU faculty and staff should exercise it and opt out of such use.
units.why: "Where that option is available, YU faculty and staff should exercise it and opt out of such use" asks users to opt out of training on their data (P50).

units.passage: Privacy violation : Users have no control over the data they provide to an AI tool. Feeding these tools with sensitive information that could lead to privacy violations must be avoided.
units.why: "Feeding these tools with sensitive information that could lead to privacy violations must be avoided" is a privacy rule (P50).
